UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile information on the ColorCanvas platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

username.description: The unique username chosen by the user.

email.description: The user's email address. Used for display; authentication is handled by an external system.

profileImageUrl.description: URL to the user's profile image stored in Firebase Storage.

bio.description: A short biographical description provided by the user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

Artwork.title: Artwork
Artwork.description: Represents an uploaded piece of artwork or content shared by a user on ColorCanvas.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Artwork entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who uploaded this artwork. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Artwork)

imageURL.description: URL to the artwork image stored in Firebase Storage.

description.description: A detailed description of the artwork.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the artwork was uploaded.

likesCount.description: The total number of likes received by this artwork.

tags.description: An array of tags or categories associated with the artwork, potentially AI-suggested.

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description: Represents a comment made by a user on an artwork.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Comment entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who made this comment. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Comment)

artworkId.description: Reference to the Artwork on which this comment was made. (Relationship: Artwork 1:N Comment)

text.description: The actual text content of the comment.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the comment was posted.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The document ID `{userId}` matches the Firebase Auth UID. Read access is public for certain fields; write access is restricted to the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`).

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user, matching their Firebase Auth UID.

definition.description: Stores artwork content uploaded by users. Documents are publicly readable (for Homepage/Explore). Write/update/delete access is restricted to the owner based on the denormalized 'userId' field in the document itself.

params.name: artworkId
params.description: The unique ID of the artwork.

definition.description: Stores comments made on a specific artwork. Documents are publicly readable. Write/update/delete access is restricted to the commenter based on the denormalized 'userId' field in the document itself. Includes denormalized 'artworkId' and 'userId' for authorization independence.

params.name: artworkId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent artwork.

params.name: commentId
params.description: The unique ID of the comment.

definition.description: A subcollection to record user likes on an artwork. Each document's ID, '{likerId}', corresponds to the `userId` of the user who liked the artwork. The document itself acts as a marker. This structure enables atomic authorization checks for liking/unliking by checking `request.auth.uid == likerId`.

params.name: artworkId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent artwork being liked.

params.name: likerId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who liked the artwork, matching their Firebase Auth UID.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for ColorCanvas prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the core design principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and consistent Access Modeling.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
1.  **User Profiles (`/userProfiles/{userId}`):** Each user's profile document ID directly corresponds to their Firebase Authentication `uid`. This ensures that authorization for profile modifications is atomic and clear: `allow write: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. The document itself contains all necessary information for its own security context.
2.  **Artworks (`/artworks/{artworkId}`):** Each `Artwork` document includes a denormalized `userId` field, explicitly linking it to its owner. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls to a parent `userProfiles` document to determine ownership, making rule evaluation atomic and efficient (e.g., `allow write: if request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId;`). This also enables atomic creation of artworks.
3.  **Comments (`/artworks/{artworkId}/comments/{commentId}`):** Similarly, each `Comment` document contains a `userId` field to identify the commenter. This denormalization allows for independent and atomic authorization checks directly on the comment document: `allow write: if request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId;`. The `artworkId` is part of the document path, providing its context without requiring a `get()` call.
4.  **Likes (`/artworks/{artworkId}/likes/{likerId}`):** To track likes without complex lookups, a dedicated subcollection `likes` is created under each artwork. The document ID for a 'like' entry is the `likerId` (the `userId` of the person who liked the artwork). This structure inherently provides authorization independence for like operations: `allow create, delete: if request.auth.uid == likerId;`. The existence of such a document signifies a like, and its atomic creation/deletion is straightforward.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters) & Structural Segregation:**
1.  **`/userProfiles/{userId}`:** This collection stores individual user profiles. While a user's *own* profile is writable only by them, public-facing fields (username, profileImageUrl, bio) are generally readable by all. The homogeneous security posture is that all documents are readable, but writes are restricted by `userId`. This supports direct access (`get`) to profiles and eliminates the need for server-side filtering on read.
2.  **`/artworks/{artworkId}`:** This collection is designed for broad public consumption (e.g., Homepage, Explore Page). All `Artwork` documents share a public read security posture, allowing `list` queries to fetch data without complex security rule filtering (e.g., `allow read: true;`). Write, update, and delete operations are restricted to the artwork's `userId` field, ensuring owner-only modification. This directly enables QAPs for efficient public listing.
3.  **`/artworks/{artworkId}/comments/{commentId}`:** This subcollection stores comments for a specific artwork. All comments for a given artwork are publicly readable. This allows for efficient `list` queries for comments under an artwork without rule-based filtering. Write/update/delete operations are restricted to the `userId` in the comment document.
4.  **`/artworks/{artworkId}/likes/{likerId}`:** This subcollection records individual likes. While listing all likers for an artwork is possible, the primary use case is to check if a specific user has liked an artwork (e.g., `get(/artworks/$(artworkId)/likes/$(request.auth.uid)).exists()`). This supports QAPs for `exists()` checks and ensures users can only create/delete their own like entries. All documents here represent a user's like, sharing the same security profile for write access.
